note: Per-table ball palette, LABELLED BY EYE from a zoomed grid of every ball on the table at t=40.01 (before any pot). Colours are the glare-trimmed crop median at that instant; white_frac is the 0.95-disc white fraction. This is truth-side data for tools/build_naming_truth.py - it is NOT installed into the engine.
not_scored_why: The crimson 3 and the orange 5 are only 23.3 Lab apart on this table, and centroids measured at one instant cannot separate them across the clip's lighting: adjudicated by eye, all 66 'truth 3 / app 5' disagreements were MY truth being wrong and the engine being right. A yardstick abstains rather than guesses, so this pair is excluded from naming truth here. Separating them needs centroids sampled per ball across many positions, which needs a way to follow each ball that does not come from the app.
revised_round63: 13 -> 9. The stripe was called a 13 (orange stripe) on the strength of it looking amber next to the BENCH's yellow 9. That is a cross-table comparison and it is invalid: under THIS table's light its own 1 reads amber too (G/R 0.676). Measured WITHIN the table, the stripe's band sits 10.0 Lab from this table's 1 and 98.8 from its 5, so by 'stripe = solid + 8' it is the 9. The same test on the bench returns 1 -> 9, which is the known answer there, so the method is validated on a case with truth. The engine had been right all along and my file was scoring it wrong 61 times.
